A narrow cobblestone road bends gently through a bright, stylized old European street. Two continuous rows of tightly packed two- and three-story buildings follow its curve, with slim brick-paved sidewalks and raised curb strips along both sides. Roughly fifteen adjoining façades face the street, their widths and setbacks varying organically.

Saturated yellow, orange, red, cream, green, and exposed dark brick give the corridor a warm, cheerful, slightly polished mood. Stucco or masonry walls carry stone-textured lower courses and window surrounds, tiled overhanging roofs, tall rectangular windows, occasional green shutters, small wrought-iron balconies, storefront-like openings, and several heavy wooden doors within rounded stone arches.

Ornate black wall lanterns recur at regular intervals; freestanding multi-lamp streetlights line the sidewalks, and drainpipes descend several façades. People, vehicles, and vegetation are absent. The dense corridor bends toward a larger brick building at one end, while the other opens abruptly onto a flat dark horizon beneath a vivid blue, cloud-dappled sky.
